And his forces: Goliath’s accompanying army, whom they face.
They said: introducing the forces’ appeal to their Lord.
Our Lord: their address when asking for patience, steadfastness, and help.
Pour out: asking for abundant patience through the image of pouring.
Patience and self-restraint: remaining steadfast under the pressure of facing the enemy.

Our feet or steps: the footing they ask to be made firm.
And help us: asking for support and victory against the opposing forces.
The people or group: the opposing community in this scene.
Those who practice kufr: describing the opposing group in this context.
Sent down: the reassurance and security that came upon them after distress.
After: marking reassurance as following distress in time.
Overwhelming distress: the condition after which reassurance is described.
Reassurance and a sense of security, further described through drowsiness.
Drowsiness: the light sleepiness overtaking a group of them.
Overtook or covered: the drowsiness enveloping one group.
A group of you: those overtaken by drowsiness.
And another group: contrasted with the first through their concern for themselves.
Had preoccupied them: engrossing their attention and anxiety.
Their own selves: their persons and lives, with which this group was preoccupied.
They supposed: their judgment about The God is described in what follows.
Other than or contrary to: a supposition inconsistent with truth.
Truth: the standard with which that supposition did not accord.

Ignorance: describing a supposition grounded in unknowing and unsound judgment.

Anything or any share: asking whether any control over the affair belongs to them.
Say: directing the addressee to state the reply.
The affair: the matter of authority and control addressed in the reply.
All of it: the whole of the affair or authority concerned.
They conceal: keeping matters within themselves without expressing them.
Within themselves: the inward setting of their concealed thought and speech.
They do not disclose: withholding from the addressee what they keep within.
They say: introducing their claim about having control and not being killed.
Had been: within the hypothetical claim of having some control over the affair.
The affair or control at issue, repeated in their claim.
Anything or a share: their hypothetical portion of control or decision.
We would not have been killed: a passive form within the group’s hypothetical claim.
Say: directing the reply concerning remaining in the houses.
You had been: the hypothetical presence of the addressees in their houses.
Your houses: the location assumed in the conditional clause.
Would surely have come forth: the verb precedes its plural subject and concerns leaving houses for the specified resting places.
Had been prescribed or recorded: a passive form concerning the killing of the people specified.
Being killed: what had been prescribed for those people.
Their places of falling: the image of resting places in the context of being killed.
And so that He may test: examining what is within your breasts.
Your breasts: here, the place through which inward matters are expressed.

Your hearts: the center of inward orientations and conditions in this expression.
Knowing: describing the awareness of The God of what is within breasts.
Breasts: with dhāt, referring to their inward contents and secrets.
And they say: their verbal profession of obedience before the addressee.
Obedience: the profession of compliance quoted from them.
They leave: departing from the addressee’s presence; the verb itself does not mean exposing hypocrisy.
Secretly plans: a group plots after leaving, contrary to the addressee’s words.
A group of them: this clause does not identify every individual as the planner.
Other than or contrary to: the difference between their secret plan and the addressee’s words.
You say: the statement with which their plan is inconsistent.
Records: The God writes down their secret planning.
They secretly plan: the schemes whose being recorded is stated.
So turn away: the instruction to turn from them.
And place your trust: relying on The God in the face of their conduct.
And is sufficient: expressing the adequacy of The God as trustee.
A trustee: one to whom affairs are entrusted and on whom reliance is placed.
They came forth: all are present and exposed before The God in the Resurrection scene.
All together: the comprehensive appearance of those in the scene.
Then said: introducing the weak group’s words to the arrogant.
The weak: followers who then question their leaders’ ability to save them.
Acted arrogantly: those whom the followers address in the exchange.
We were: stating their former relationship of following them.
Followers: those who had followed those leaders.
Able to avert or relieve: asking whether they can remove any punishment from them.
Punishment: the suffering and punitive consequence described in the scene.
Anything or any amount: whatever part of the punishment they ask to have averted.
They said: the arrogant leaders’ reply to their followers.
Had guided us: within the conditional reply quoted from them.
We would have guided you too: the consequence of the condition in their own statement.
It is the same: panic and patience have the same outcome for them in that situation.
Whether we panic: one side of the contrast between distress and patience.
We remain patient: the other side of the same contrast.
An escape: the exchange ends by stating that they have no way out.

Is changed or replaced: a passive form concerning the earth.
The earth: what is first identified as undergoing change.
Other or different: distinguishing the changed earth from the one mentioned.
The earth: in ghayra al-arḍ, the reference against which difference is expressed.

The One: describing the oneness of The God.
The Overpowering: describing the encompassing mastery of The God.

We set in motion: moving or driving the mountains.
The mountains: what is said to be set in motion.

The day when: the time of their being exposed in the scene.

Sovereignty or dominion: the subject of the question, to whom does it belong today?
Today: the day described in the judgment scene.
The One: describing the oneness of The God.
The Overpowering: describing the mastery and sovereignty of The God.
Was made manifest: the passive form describing Hell being exposed to view.
Hell: what is made visible in this sentence.
